one_liner.text: An AI thinking partner that remembers how an idea evolved and turns that context into something the user can keep building on.

description.text: A Next.js thinking-partner app that keeps conversations, ideas, a versioned context brief, and durable memories so later turns can continue from where the thinking stands.

evidence.excerpt: Frimz helps people develop ideas over time
Add Frimz, a thinking partner that remembers how ideas evolve.

problem.text: Useful thinking appears in a conversation, then the chat ends and the path — decisions, rejections, open questions — is hard to reuse, so the user has to re-explain the idea.

solution.text: Each turn resolves an idea, recalls durable memories, loads a living context brief, chooses a conversation strategy, streams a reply, and can later extract memories or draft a write-up from that picture.

users.text: Founders, developers, marketers, researchers, students, and anyone developing a project that does not fit in one chat.

description.text: Each user message is classified into an intent, thinking stage, and conversational move so the agent explores, challenges, confirms, drafts, or answers instead of treating every turn the same.

journeys.name: Signed-in chat turn
beats: POST /api/chat with message and optional mode
Persist the user message unless retrying
Resolve or attach the current idea
Load the idea brief if one exists
Choose a conversation strategy and stream tokens
Emit done with optional indicators and draft metadata

beats: Client sends retry:true with a conversationId
Delete the last assistant message if present

claim.text: A conversation can regenerate the last assistant reply from the previous user message.

journeys.name: Return and continue an idea
beats: Keep durable memories and a living brief
Come back in a later conversation
Optionally turn the brief into a written draft

architecture.text: Next.js 15 App Router Node server. POST /api/chat authenticates, rate-limits, and streams runChatTurn. The agent resolves an idea, recalls memories via PostgresMemoryIndex plus optional Walrus, loads a context brief, builds prompts with a conversation strategy, and calls getLLMProvider. Durable app state lives in Postgres; semantic memory blobs are intended for Walrus and catalogued in memory_index. Production is a standalone Node image.

stack.text: Next.js 15.5.4 App Router with React 19.1.1 and TypeScript 5.9
PostgreSQL accessed through Drizzle ORM and the postgres.js client
Tailwind CSS 4 with Radix UI primitives, lucide-react, next-themes, and sonner
Vitest for unit tests; ESLint via eslint-config-next

dependencies.text: @cursor/sdk ^1.0.34 is a runtime LLM/provider dependency, marked external for the standalone server.
@mysten-incubation/memwal ^0.1.8 is the Walrus memory client used for semantic recall.
@mysten/sui ^2.33.2 and @mysten/seal ^1.4.17 are bundled into the standalone trace.
next-auth ^5.0.0-beta.29 plus bcryptjs for credential-style user records.
zod for request validation; react-markdown, remark-gfm, and rehype-sanitize for rendered markdown.

claim.text: Chat and extraction go through getLLMProvider from the Cursor provider.
Semantic memory search is delegated to getMemoryStore(); failures are logged as walrus_recall_failed and the turn continues with preference rows only.
Sui and Seal packages are production dependencies and included in standalone file tracing; no on-chain call sites appear in this evidence pack.
Chat requires a current user; users and sessions tables plus next-auth/bcryptjs indicate password-backed account sessions.
Local compose runs Postgres 16 as database frimz on host port 5436.

Authenticated JSON POST that streams SSE events (conversation, token, done, error). Accepts conversationId, message, mode, and retry. Rejects anonymous users (401), invalid/empty messages (400), and rate-limited users (429). Node runtime, force-dynamic, maxDuration 300.

database.text: Drizzle Postgres schema includes users, sessions, ideas, conversations, messages, user_settings, and memory_index. Context briefs are typed against ContextBriefData and loaded per idea; the brief table itself is truncated in this pack.

auth.text: Chat requires a signed-in user via requireUser. Accounts store unique email and a password hash; sessions have a token and expiry. Git notes Edge auth middleware was removed so Vercel signup would not crash loading middleware.js as CommonJS.

evidence.excerpt: Drop the Edge auth middleware so Vercel signup no longer crashes

deployment.text: Production image is a multi-stage Node 22 standalone Next server (node server.js, HOSTNAME 0.0.0.0, EXPOSE 3000). Vercel is documented as deploying Dockerfile.vercel and keeping a long-running Node process. Local Postgres is compose-managed. Security headers apply to all paths.

implemented_functionality.text: Regex intent analyzer maps phrases to signals such as reset, return_idea, switch_topic, mind_change, fed_up, excited, and others.

Strategy tests lock behaviors: create space for unformed ideas, confirm decisions, reconstruct history only from stored memories, honor exclusions, answer definitions shortly, synthesize when lost, and draft without extra questions.
Per-user chat rate limiting returns 429 with a pause message.
Brief text/list/reasoned fields are cleaned, de-duplicated, length-capped, and placeholder values are dropped.
The orchestrator is set up to extract memories with MEMORY_EXTRACTION_PROMPT, validate them, optionally create idea events, and plan memory writes.
All routes send framing denial, nosniff, strict-origin referrer, and disabled camera/microphone/geolocation permissions. Header names are redacted in the pack.
Per-user display name and theme (default system) are stored in user_settings.
